picks.title: Authors paid hundreds to publish their books, but allege 'crap' service and AI art
picks.excerpt: Authors accuse paid-publishing service Patrick White Publishing of poor service and AI-generated cover/staff imagery; ABC found AI-generated images in its staff profiles.
picks.rationale: An original ABC investigation into a paid-publishing service: authors say they paid for poor service and AI covers, and ABC found AI-generated faces in the company's staff profiles. Self-publishing authors can use it as a checklist for vetting a vendor.

picks.title: AI-Assisted Paper on Z-Library Cites a TorrentFreak Article That Doesn't Exist
picks.excerpt: An academic paper on the Z-Library shadow library, written with disclosed AI help, cites a nonexistent TorrentFreak article and other unfindable sources.
picks.rationale: A new, checkable case: a peer-reviewed paper about Z-Library that disclosed AI help cites a TorrentFreak article that does not exist. It shows that disclosing AI use does not catch hallucinated citations, which matters to editors and scholarly publishers.

picks.title: Publishers rely on trust, not tech, to ensure books aren't AI-generated
picks.excerpt: With AI detectors unreliable, Canadian publishers such as Coach House Books say they ask writers to disclose AI-generated material and rely on trust.
picks.rationale: Shows how Canadian presses such as Coach House actually screen manuscripts for AI: detectors are unreliable, so they rely on author disclosure clauses and trust. It is a working practice other presses can copy.

picks.title: 370 Books In 20 Months Has Made This Author Famous For All The Wrong Reasons
picks.excerpt: South African romance writer Coral Hart says she has published 370+ books with AI since February 2025, drawing backlash and threats and reigniting the authorship debate.
picks.rationale: Shows what AI-volume publishing looks like in practice: romance author Coral Hart says she has released 370+ AI-assisted books in 20 months, which helps explain the KDP flood and the human-authorship labels.

picks.title: From Content to Trusted Knowledge: Reflections on Frankfurt Book Fair 2026
picks.excerpt: Frankfurt 2026 takeaways on how publishers turn trusted content into usable knowledge as AI answer engines and agents become the reading interface.
picks.rationale: A strategy takeaway from Frankfurt: as AI answer engines and agents become the way people read, publishers need to package trusted content as usable knowledge, not just sell files. It comes from an independent industry blog, not a vendor.
